processAdapter.entry: encoded.cjs creates an owned process; host.cjs alone loads the RTC addon. Direct node signatures below describe the child N-API layer.
processAdapter.asynchronous: request/respond, media submission, audio metadata and frame release await correlated child results. cancel is bounded dispatch; the original request remains the completion proof. Audio probes use the existing native RTC clock, with no timestamp substitution.
processAdapter.bounds: 128 outstanding calls, 32MiB serialized pending data, 16 encoded admission requests, 8 PCM processing requests; production capture additionally retains only one AU awaiting admission. At most 128 unacknowledged native events/8MiB. Budget exhaustion rejects, never creates an unbounded queue.
processAdapter.textures: Kernel-only helper pins the actual process object and duplicates its NT HANDLE into the importer. Main owns each duplicate until Chromium retirement or unused proof. Original native GPU retirement is awaited while alive; on actual host death OS disposal is distinguished from GPU fence completion. Legacy input GPU texture loans remain guarded after host death without a reader/fence receipt; full-close proof then rejects. Production screen publication uses compressed bytes, not these input GPU loans.
processAdapter.snapshot: snapshot() returns a copied cached observation with explicit process metadata; refreshSnapshot() awaits a real child observation. close() proves OS exit and all Main texture duplicates retired, not merely a native close response.
processAdapter.capabilities: Synchronous compiled capabilities come from the hash-verified build manifest. The child validates its actual DLL against that complete declaration before ready resolves; neither is a hardware probe.

node.capabilities: () -> actual DLL implementation surface; no hardware/device probe; revision8 adds H264 Level6 and an 80Mbps ceiling with profile-dependent negotiation, retaining expected-epoch admission and owner-scoped audio, stereo and retirement guarantees
node.createEngine: (options, onEvent) -> engine; await engine.ready; loader and addon require DLL-advertised ABI2/contractRevision8/audioExtensionVersion1, audioAvailable and requiredCompiledCapabilities BEFORE native creation
node.options: {maxResources?:32 (1..64),maxPendingOperations?:64 (1..128),maxDecodedFrames?:16 (1..64),operationTimeoutMs?:12000 (100..60000),maximumH264Level?:52 (31|32|40|41|42|50|51|52|60),requireAudio?:false}; unknown options reject before creation; requireAudio means compiled support, never hardware qualification
node.submitFrame: engine.submitFrame(sourceId, {frameId, handle:Buffer[8], timestampUs, durationUs, ntpTimeMs}) -> Promise<{sourceId,frameId,ok:true}>; resolves actual input retirement, not C admission or network delivery. No enabled video sinks and transient per-frame clock rejection retire unused, counted in source.droppedNoSinks/droppedClock without publication. A slightly early original compositor PTS may wait once on the interruptible source worker, bounded by one configured frame interval and10ms; strict mapping is retried only after actual time advances. Waits/interrupted waits are observable, never publication proof. Clock discontinuity/reset-required failures remain terminal; timestamps are never retimed
node.submitAudioPacket: engine.submitAudioPacket(sourceId, originalCapturePacket) -> Promise<{sourceId,epoch,sequence,frameIndex,frames,ok:true}>; original non-shared Float32LE Buffer copied synchronously at C admission; Promise tracks processing, not an asynchronous JS-memory loan or RTP delivery
node.grantAudioCredits: engine.grantAudioCredits({epoch,grantSequence,frames:480|960}) -> void; direct bounded admission, throws on failure
node.audioClockProbe: engine.audioClockProbe({epoch,probeId}) -> {epoch,probeId,rtcBeforeUs,rtcAfterUs}; native retains its genuine RTC readings; no renderer-supplied native time
node.calibrateAudioClock: engine.calibrateAudioClock({epoch,probeId,rendererBeforeUs,rendererAfterUs}) -> {epoch,calibrationId,offsetUs,uncertaintyUs}; consumes owned probe, renderer records the real performance-clock roundtrip bracket
node.releaseFrame: engine.releaseFrame(frameId, 'unused'|'all-references-released') -> Promise<frame.released.data>; duplicate releases reject. 'unused' is only for frames never imported externally.
node.snapshot: engine.snapshot(); audio.outputConfigured describes a valid owned native output, independent of audio.playing (RTC activity); neither proves physical device health or leases admission. peers/sfu/mf are actor observations, not atomic RTCStats; peer.getStats/sfu.getStats collect real stats. mf.encoders keeps configured/requested rates and real core counters/queue/encode latency separate per live worker sessionId. hardwareAdvertised/lowLatencyConfigured are MFT metadata, never physical hardware execution proof. mf.rtcRejectedAccessUnits counts documented RTC send refusals, including an AU already in flight at Stop; they retain keyframe recovery without becoming codec failures
node.close: engine.close() -> Promise<snapshot>; timeout retains native ownership

commands.source.createAudio: target=0; {sessionId,syncGroup,format:{sampleRate,channels,channelMask,sourceBitsPerSample,sourceValidBitsPerSample}} -> {sourceId,kind:'audio'}; one local audio capture source per engine, default disabled, no native device capture
commands.source.beginAudioEpoch: target=audioSourceId; {epoch,firstSequence,firstFrameIndex,format} -> {sourceId,epoch}; fences admitted old packets before resetting the continuous resampler to an explicit real capture generation
commands.source.setAudioSyncGroup: target=audioSourceId; {syncGroup} -> {sourceId,syncGroup}; requires no live publications; does not mutate MSID on an existing SSRC
commands.audio.configureOutput: target=0; {epoch} -> {epoch,sampleRate:48000,channels:2}; owner already selected/started the exact Chromium output; new logical epoch requires prior output retirement, not merely RTC pause. No native device opens
commands.audio.stopOutput: target=0; {epoch} -> {}; fences playout callbacks and retires that epoch's clock/grants/CPU copies. Idempotent after ADM epoch0, but an old request cannot stop a different active epoch (ERR_RTC_ARGUMENT/status1). Not global engine/GPU retirement
commands.source.setEnabled: target=sourceId; {enabled} -> {enabled}; also gates every publication of that source
commands.peer.setLocalDescription: target=peerId; {type:'offer'|'answer',sdp,expectedOutputEpoch?:positiveSafeInteger} -> {}; expectedOutputEpoch REQUIRED for active audio recvonly/sendrecv
commands.peer.setRemoteDescription: target=peerId; {type:'offer'|'answer',sdp,expectedOutputEpoch?:positiveSafeInteger} -> {}; active audio requires Opus48k/2; expectedOutputEpoch REQUIRED for active audio sendonly/sendrecv
commands.peer.publish: target=peerId; {sourceId,enabled?:false,maxBitrateBps,maxFramerate} -> {publicationId,kind:'video',trackId,mid:null|string,streamIds:string[]}; source.syncGroup is MSID, independent of peer scope
commands.peer.publishAudio: target=peerId; {sourceId,enabled?:false,maxBitrateBps:6000..510000} -> publication metadata with kind:'audio'; one local audio publication per peer, dedicated SENDONLY transceiver and Opus codec preferences
commands.peer.setReceiverVolume: target=peerId; {receiverId,volume:0..2} -> {receiverId,receiverEpoch,volume}; audio-only remote source gain before shared mixing; preserves independent authorization/watch gates
commands.peer.setPublicationEnabled: target=publicationId; {enabled} -> {enabled}; encoding.active, never synthetic black frames
commands.peer.setReceiving: target=peerId; {enabled,expectedOutputEpoch?:positiveSafeInteger} -> {enabled,renegotiationRequired:boolean}; expectedOutputEpoch required when enabling a present individually authorized audio receiver, and must equal that receiver's prepared epoch. Aggregate anyWatched(video OR audio), with separate default-disabled individual receiver authorization
commands.peer.setReceiverEnabled: target=peerId; {receiverId,enabled,expectedOutputEpoch?:positiveSafeInteger} -> {receiverId,receiverEpoch,enabled,requestedEnabled}; expectedOutputEpoch required when enabling audio, validated before and after gate effects. requestedEnabled echoes the individual request; enabled is effective and also requires a present binding and the aggregate peer.setReceiving gate
commands.peer.getStats: target=peerId; {} -> direct real RTCStats array; empty native string normalizes to []; top-level timestamp remains microseconds
commands.sfu.load: target=0; {routerRtpCapabilities,iceServers?:[]} -> {deviceId,rtpCapabilities,canProduceVideo,canProduceAudio}; router intersection, not an audio device probe
commands.sfu.produce: target=transportId; {sourceId,enabled?:false,maxBitrateBps,maxFramerate?:videoOnly,appData:{mediaType:'screen_video'|'screen_audio',syncGroup}} -> {producerId,serverProducerId,kind,syncGroup}; appData must match actual source kind/group; one screen audio producer
commands.sfu.consume: target=transportId; {id,producerId,kind:'video'|'audio',rtpParameters,appData:{mediaType:'screen_video'|'screen_audio',syncGroup},enabled?:false,expectedOutputEpoch?:positiveSafeInteger} -> {consumerId,serverConsumerId,kind,syncGroup,mid,trackId}; expectedOutputEpoch REQUIRED for audio even initially disabled. mid is nonempty string (explicit ASCII1..64), never null; trackId is actual nonempty MSID track identifier (ASCII1..256 in this SDK path). Server consumer paused before SDP; close old audio consumer before rebinding same producer
commands.sfu.setConsumerVolume: target=audioConsumerId; {volume:0..2} -> {consumerId,volume}; remote source gain before mixer, effective zero while consumer is disabled
commands.sfu.setProducerEnabled: target=producerId; {enabled:requested} -> {enabled:effective}; effective=requested&&sourceEnabled, same effective boolean in callback. Requested intention persists natively across source gates; no requestedEnabled DTO field
commands.sfu.setConsumerEnabled: target=consumerId; {enabled,expectedOutputEpoch?:positiveSafeInteger} -> {enabled}; expectedOutputEpoch required when enabling audio and compared before server/local effects and after acknowledgement. Callback and successful result reflect the requested boolean, independent of local source gates
commands.sfu.getStats: target=transportId|producerId|consumerId; {} -> direct RTCStats array, top-level timestamp remains microseconds
commands.resource.close: target=sourceId|peerId|publicationId|deviceId|transportId|producerId|consumerId; {}; unknown IDs, nonempty data and sources in use reject before cancelling other work. Concurrent admitted closes succeed if that known resource was already retired. Native/local only: no server pause/delete acknowledgement is requested.

events.ready: target=0; data={capabilities}; real factory initialization succeeded
events.peer.state: target=peerId; partial patch with exactly one string field: signalingState OR iceConnectionState OR connectionState OR iceGatheringState; merge patches
events.peer.trackAdded: target=peerId; data={receiverId,receiverEpoch,kind:'video'|'audio',trackId,mid:null|string,streamIds:string[],reason?}; stable receiver identity with a default-disabled binding, including reattachment
events.peer.trackUpdated: target=peerId; same metadata as peer.trackAdded; emitted before new-epoch frames on authorization/aggregate-gate/track/MID/stream changes
events.peer.trackRemoved: target=peerId; same receiver metadata; route invalidated but live Unified Plan receiver/history retained until peer teardown; exposed GPU leases remain independently owned
events.peer.publicationUpdated: target=peerId; data={publicationId,kind:'video'|'audio',trackId,mid:null|string,streamIds:string[]}; real sender metadata refreshed after SDP completion
events.frame: target=peerId|consumerId; data={frameId,routeKind:'peer'|'consumer',receiverId?:number,receiverEpoch?:number,width,height,codedWidth,codedHeight,timestampUs,format:'NV12',gpuCopy:true,textureInfo:{pixelFormat:'nv12',handle:{ntHandle:Buffer[8]},codedSize:{width,height},visibleRect:{x,y,width,height},timestamp:us,colorSpace:{primaries:'bt709',transfer:'bt709',matrix:'bt709',range:'limited'}}}; peer requires receiverId/receiverEpoch; consumer omits them; real single-slice export with completed native GPU copy
events.frame.released: target=peerId|consumerId; data={frameId,ok,error?}; actual native GPU lease retirement, after external-reference proof, AcquireSync(0) and the reclamation fence
events.source.frameReleased: target=sourceId; data={sourceId,frameId,ok,error?}; actual reader and native admission retirement, including ok:false; producer lease may now be released
events.source.audioPacketReleased: target=audioSourceId; data={sourceId,epoch,sequence,frameIndex,frames,ok,error?}; retires native packet work, not source-owned partial SRC history; malformed/lost processing completion waits for validated retirement or complete close
events.audio.playout: target=0; data={epoch,sequence,firstPlayoutFrame,frames:480,sampleRate:48000,channels:2,samples:Float32Array[960]}; actual mixed CPU PCM copied through audio extension1, never JSON-encoded or fabricated after a stale read
events.audio.outputInvalidated: target=0; data={epoch:positiveSafeInteger,reason:'owner-stop'|'engine-close'|'transport-detached'|'setup-failed'|'mixer-failure'}; typed C SIGNAL event for actual owned-output retirement only. Normal RTC StopPlayout pauses and emits NOTHING. Captured retired epoch, never snapshot0. Multiple causes can notify E; handle idempotently. Late E never invalidates E+1
events.audio.outputError: target=0; data={epoch:capturedFailingEpoch,code:'ERR_RTC_AUDIO_OUTPUT',message:'Audio output epoch failed; select/recreate a new output epoch',status:7,hresult:0,terminal:false}; mixer/output failure only, no reason field. Epoch-scoped cleanup and invalidation precede this diagnostic; never resume an old anchor
events.error: target=resource or 0; data={code,message,status,hresult,terminal,adapterSessionId?,codecStatus?}; MF session IDs are not engine resource IDs; an unmapped terminal MF failure closes the native screen engine
events.closed: target=0; actual thread/source/MF/decoded-lease retirement, never merely a stop request

audio.binaryAbi: audio/monky_rtc_audio.h extension1: input POD384 bytes, output POD3904, fixed metadata reply POD4112; old ABI2 PODs unchanged; no STL/foreign allocator ownership crosses C
audio.capturePacket: {sessionId,pcm:Buffer Float32LE interleaved,format:{encoding:'float32-interleaved',sampleRate,channels,channelMask,sourceBitsPerSample,sourceValidBitsPerSample},frames,sequence,frameIndex,epoch,devicePosition:number|null,qpcTimestampUs:number|null,flags:{raw,silent,dataDiscontinuity,timestampError}}; unrequested process-loopback devicePosition is null independently of valid QPC, represented by UINT64_MAX in the unchanged C/POD. TIMESTAMP_ERROR requires both anchors absent; QPC absence without that actual flag rejects. A supplied device position of zero remains a real counter, not an unavailable sentinel
audio.formats: 8000/16000/24000/32000/44100/48000/88200/96000/192000 Hz; mono mask null/0/4 explicitly duplicated, stereo mask null/0/3 preserved at unchanged gain; 6-channel 5.1 requires Windows mask 0x3f or 0x60f, 8-channel 7.1 requires 0x63f (1599). Ascending Windows speaker-bit order is explicit; absent/zero multichannel masks, mismatched counts and other layouts/rates reject
audio.normalization: Continuous pinned WebRTC PushResampler per explicit epoch, not per packet. Surround first uses M140 ChannelMixingMatrix reordered to Windows speaker order in floating point: FL/FR to their own side, center/LFE to both and surrounds to their own side at 1/sqrt(2), no LFE boost/filter. Fixed shared headroom 1/(1+3/sqrt(2)) for 5.1 and 1/(1+4/sqrt(2)) for 7.1 also attenuates front-only content (-9.89/-11.66 dB); no dynamic gain. One final signed16 conversion, with out-of-range/SRC overshoot counted in clippedSamples. Original format/packet positions/QPC/flags remain in epoch/block provenance; no added delay/frames. Stereo 48k 480-frame OnData reaches only that source's track sinks; CPU controls do not qualify physical stereo/audibility
audio.stereo: Factory encoder/decoder capabilities advertise stereo=1 and sprop-stereo=1 because M140 codec preferences select existing supported FMTP rather than copying arbitrary preference parameters. Encoder configuration rejects mono negotiation. SFU Produce passes opusStereo:true to the actual SDK answer generator. Opus remains lossy/adaptive; this is negotiated stereo, not a lossless quality guarantee
audio.captureTime: Original QPC plus exact input-sample offset minus pinned 16-input-frame SRC delay when resampling maps through the engine-shared paired clock; AudioTrackSinkInterface absolute timestamp is RTC TimeMillis, NOT NTP. Pre-epoch priming and timestamp-error packets have no invented anchor
audio.inputBounds: 8 pending native packets/Node processing promises, at most 1MiB each; C copies synchronously. Duplicate preserves the original processing obligation; malformed/lost retirement retains the ledger until valid retirement or wait_closed/destroy+TSFN drain. Correlated errors carry nativeOwnershipRetained:false and processingPending; this is separate from GPU lease ownership
audio.epochs: A source accepts only its explicit current real capture epoch. beginAudioEpoch disables admission and fences old packet work before restarting DSP. Stale epochs reject before queueing and cannot poison the new SRC. Supplied device counters advance exactly by prior frames; absent/present counter transitions, original discontinuity flags, QPC regressions/validity changes and gaps require a new epoch. Without a counter, QPC/sample gap or overlap exceeding ceil(2000000/sampleRate)+1 microseconds (two input frames plus rounding slack) rejects until a new actual epoch. No timestamp correction, invented flags, synthetic counter or replay/padding of PCM
audio.outputBounds: One engine mixer and credit-driven native worker, no extra pacing timer. Credits are consecutive grantSequence starting1, frames480|960, epoch positive safe strictly advancing; capacity1920 frames/4 output packets. Packets have sequence starting0 and actual firstPlayoutFrame starting0, increment480
audio.physicalClock: Native owns probe readings; renderer echoes actual performance-clock bracket. Probe budget16, native span<=20ms, renderer RTT<=8ms, uncertainty half both spans plus16ms<=20ms, freshness200ms, offset discontinuity<=100ms. Feedback must reference exact epoch/calibration, monotonic worklet epoch and real confirmedPcmEnd<=native mixed cursor
audio.playoutDelay: ADM delay is ceil((actual mixed cursor-physically played estimate)*1000/48000) from current calibrated feedback. estimatedPlayoutFrame is finite and signed, bounded below by -Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and above by confirmedPcmEnd; legitimate pre-anchor negatives and fractions are preserved, never clamped. No second baseLatency/outputLatency, no extrapolation past confirmedPcmEnd, no fabricated zero/constant delay. Missing/stale/uncertain or uint16-millisecond-unrepresentable delay returns unavailable
audio.outputLifecycle: One global owner per engine. Normal RTC StopPlayout (including last receiver removal) only pauses: preserves epoch/configuration, next packet/grant sequence, native cursor, queued PCM and unpaid credits. It finishes/delivers a reserved in-flight block before returning. Paused worker waits for playing AND credits; StartPlayout wakes it without a new grant. Only explicit audio.stopOutput, actual failure, callback detachment/setup failure or engine close retires owned output and emits audio.outputInvalidated after its fence/epoch-scoped cleanup. Late E never clears E+1. Paused configuration cannot be replaced without retirement
audio.pauseClock: The selected Renderer context belongs to the output owner, not RTC receiver count. Grants and clock metadata remain valid for a configured paused epoch; PlayoutDelay returns unavailable while paused. Renderer underrun silence is never counted as native PCM. A real gap is represented by unavailable feedback and the worklet's new clock epoch/actual PCM anchor; current calibration/freshness/confirmedPcmEnd bounds remain mandatory. Native never advances its cursor through padding or extrapolates beyond confirmed PCM, and never fabricates an anchor on resume
audio.outputErrors: Direct grant/probe/calibrate/feedback with retired/wrong output epoch: ERR_RTC_AUDIO_OUTPUT_EPOCH/status2; pause alone is NOT this error. Invalid sequence/capacity/stale calibration/feedback, or retirement racing the entry guard: ERR_RTC_AUDIO/status1. Neither generic status1/2 nor a late command for E proves E+1 retired

admission.notALease: prepareOutput success, outputConfigured/OutputReady and invalidation delivery are observations, not atomic leases or physical qualification. Readiness means owned configuration, not playing. Last-receiver removal cannot invalidate that configuration between JS preflight and admission; explicit stop/failure still can.
admission.expectedEpoch: Receiving public SDP and audio sfu.consume require expectedOutputEpoch, a positive safe integer copied from the owned output selected for THIS attempt, not a JS lease. Native compares the exact epoch under its state synchronization before effects and again after entry; a ready E2 never satisfies an E1 attempt. Missing/invalid metadata rejects ERR_RTC_ARGUMENT/status1. The field is optional for nonreceiving/video-only operations but validated if supplied.
admission.serialization: ConfigureOutput, StopOutput and public SDP/consume execute on the same control actor, so configuration replacement cannot interleave inside an admitted operation. The pre-guard takes synchronized native ADM/epoch observations. A later asynchronous failure may occur between that guard and RTC/SDK invocation; crossing the guard is the conservative admission boundary, not a promise of uninterruptible physical output. Post-entry checks retain the captured expected epoch and never relabel failures as pre-admission.
admission.preMutationRetry: Only ERR_RTC_AUDIO_OUTPUT_PRE_ADMISSION/status8 from peer.setLocalDescription/peer.setRemoteDescription or entry sfu.consume proves this operation has not called RTC SetDescription, allocated a consumer/MID or emitted a server callback. Native error remains correlated by engine/requestId/target; the caller retains the exact expectedOutputEpoch of that attempt. The owner may prepare a current global output and retry IDENTICAL SDP/media/resource payload with a NEW requestId and updated expectedOutputEpoch, bounded attempts and still-current intent/peer. Do not rerun CreateOffer or create server resources. Existing parent-owned server records are not retired by this rejection. This code is never used inside the SDK after side effects begin.
admission.lateFailure: ERR_RTC_AUDIO_OUTPUT_DURING_ADMISSION/status7 or other RTC/SDK/output errors after entry do NOT permit SDP replay. The existing failed-admission path retires the affected peer/transport; server cleanup remains the parent's responsibility. Cancellation/timeout/unknown outcome likewise never proves pre-mutation.
admission.directions: Inactive/rejected audio SDP requires no output. Local recvonly/sendrecv and remote sendonly/sendrecv require it, even if individual delivery remains disabled. SFU audio consume requires output even initially paused.
admission.ordering: Last-receiver/peer/transport removal fences the RTC pause before its close acknowledgement but does not retire output or emit an output event. Explicit audio.stopOutput fences native work and clears only its epoch. Invalidation and operation completion traverse the SAME TSFN FIFO; on a healthy channel the synchronous invalidation listener runs BEFORE that operation Promise settles. It does not await returned Promises or asynchronous owner/renderer cleanup. A successful engine.close additionally waits for native retirement and queue drain; timeout, broken delivery or environment teardown do not guarantee callback delivery before rejection. Closing a SENDONLY publication only initiates retirement negotiation and proves no remote receiver/output retirement. Independent failures have no fabricated requestId/causal ordering.

audio.reassociation: P2P closes only its dedicated SENDONLY audio publication, StopStandard, negotiates until stopped, then publishes replacement with same PCM source/new group. SFU closes prior audio consumer, then consumes the SAME producer paused on the SAME receive transport with new explicit streamId; original CNAME/SSRC are untouched
audio.qualification: Compiled implementation only. Factory/device/media/AudioContext execution and physical A/V qualification are explicitly outside inert controls

decodedVideoClock.timestamp: Received timestampUs is RTC render deadline in its real clock, or 0/-1 immediate sentinel; never original QPC/MF PTS
decodedVideoClock.smoothing: Factory/PC media config preserves M140 enable_prerenderer_smoothing default true. The exporter waits for its GPU copy, not a second media rendering delay
decodedVideoClock.presentation: Use measured RTC-to-renderer calibration and only remaining deadline when integrating physical presentation; do not add a second fixed wait. Physical A/V remains unqualified

inputRetirement.unadmitted: Known sourceId/frameId, proven unadmitted: reject with nativeOwnershipRetained:false plus both IDs. Input identity is read once before readiness checks; no phase inference from SOURCE_DISABLED/CLOSED codes.
inputRetirement.duplicate: A live JS duplicate, native duplicate or reentrant admission of the same key rejects with nativeOwnershipRetained:true and preserves the existing obligation. Unknown/unsafe identity never gains invented correlation or release proof.
inputRetirement.retiredSuccess: Validated source.frameReleased ok:true resolves {sourceId,frameId,ok:true}; only ownership is proved, not successful encode/network/presentation.
inputRetirement.retiredError: Validated ok:false rejects with nativeOwnershipRetained:false plus sourceId/frameId and the visible native failure.
inputRetirement.invalidCompletion: Malformed or lost completion preserves the input ledger/deferred until validated retirement or complete close; a protocol error is surfaced and close may be requested.
inputRetirement.completeClose: Only wait_closed/destroy plus Node TSFN drain retires remaining inputs; each gets an individual error with nativeOwnershipRetained:false and its own sourceId/frameId.
inputRetirement.notProof: Terminal error, timeout, cancel(requestId), source-close request and JSON closed alone do not retire input ownership. cancel is a control-operation API, not frame cancellation.

captureClock.input: timestampUs is original WGC/QPC system-relative microseconds. GPU frame/MF PTS remain unchanged; only VideoFrame.timestamp_us is translated.
captureClock.mapping: One engine-shared mapper uses its actual WebRTC environment clock and paired QPC-before/RTC-now/QPC-after observations. TimestampAligner trains only on paired NOW observations, never frame arrival; each source has independent ordering guards.
captureClock.bounds: Sampling bracket <=2ms; RTC quantization allowance 16ms; calibration cadence 100ms; capture age <=2s; discontinuity guard 100ms and alignment-error guard 50ms. Future QPC capture is rejected; translated RTC time may lead its coarse latest tick only within 16ms plus half the measured bracket (rounded up) plus 1us. Uncertain/stale/nonmonotonic frames are explicitly dropped, never timestamp-incremented or replaced by now.
captureClock.reset: Source/clock restart or unmaintainable continuity is diagnosed and requires explicit source/engine recreation. Close shuts the shared mapper before destruction of its environment clock.
captureClock.nominalDuration: durationUs may be round(1e6/fps), integer 1..1000000, explicitly nominal rather than measured. ntpTimeMs=-1 means NTP not supplied for video-only; no fabricated NTP.

ownership.handles: Engine-local safe integer handles are monotonic and never reused; server IDs remain separate strings.
ownership.cancellation: cancel and respond never queue behind the actor. A validated, successfully admitted resource close cancels pending non-close operations targeted at it and its descendants; concurrent closes cooperate. Source users are tracked before native publication creation. Cancel pending create requests by requestId on room/scope teardown. Once completion wins the serialized native commit point, cancel returns NOT_FOUND; an accepted earlier cancellation retires late-created native resources. Do not reuse request IDs until their completion events.
ownership.input: Only a genuinely leased immutable keyed-mutex NV12 NT texture, BT.709 limited. No fabricated I420 carrier or CPU mapping. Input frameId is unique per source while retained; different sources may use the same frameId. C submit OK acknowledges admission; Node submitFrame Promise waits for the inputRetirement proof matrix.
ownership.decoded: Decoded frames are explicitly GPU-copied into bounded ArraySize=1/MipLevels=1 NV12 NT textures. The original MF buffer/readback owner remains retained until that copy fence completes, then is released independently of display latency. NT HANDLE bytes are borrowed in Main; Electron45alpha6 duplicates them. No CPU readback, fake surface, array-slice DTO or zero-copy claim.
ownership.presentationRelease: After a successful import, only Electron allReferencesReleased may authorize releaseFrame(id,'all-references-released'). IPC ACK, writer.write, closing one VideoFrame and stop are insufficient. The native worker then reacquires key 0 and observes a reclamation fence before reuse. 'unused' applies only before any external import. On timeout or ambiguous GPU ownership the lease remains retained.
ownership.presentationShutdown: Stop renderer consumption, close every VideoFrame/ImportedSharedTexture and drain real allReferencesReleased callbacks before engine.close. A delivered external lease is never auto-released by GC/environment teardown. Unreturned leases or blocked drivers can keep close/environment cleanup pending instead of unloading live resources.
ownership.nodeEventTeardown: TSFN finalization revokes producer access under the same mutex used for enqueue/release. A napi_closing return revokes the handle without another producer release. Finalizer and every accepted item own independent context refs, including fault notifications and env=null discard. The native close worker waits for observed finalization AND zero pending items before returning to the normal async completion callback; finalizers/discard do not settle JS promises or call Node APIs. Finalizer order/LIFO is never proof of drain.
ownership.watchers: Sources, publications and receiver bindings default disabled. Parent owns authenticated watcher/room signaling; screen audio gain/mute is independent from call deafen. Never route through call/microphone/camera resources.
ownership.peerRouting: Receiver IDs are engine-local never-reused identities, not generic resource.close handles. History is bounded by min(maxResources,64) per peer and retained while the native receiver lives. Epoch advances on deactivation/reactivation/binding changes; fresh or rebound/MID/stream-changed bindings require individual authorization. Metadata is emitted before sink activation. Full {peer,receiver,epoch} routes pass through engine admission, exporter and latest-frame selection. Retired routes cancel only unexposed work; exposed frames still require their original frameId release/fence protocol.
ownership.peerWatchSelection: peer.setReceiving is aggregate anyWatched(video OR audio). peer.setReceiverEnabled gates individual local delivery, not remote RTP. Per-destination peer.setPublicationEnabled controls the actual sender. source.setEnabled gates all publications of a source. Keep one PC per participant pair, not per screen.
ownership.screenIdentity: Each local screen source has a unique opaque synchronization group; the sole local audio source uses the selected screen group. Peer syncGroup is scope metadata, not a restriction on its publications. Actual source groups become sender MSID; each SFU consumer gets explicit group MSID without changing RTP CNAME/SSRC. These are not authenticated shareId values; parent maps actual source/publication/track identities.
ownership.sfuReceiveMids: Receive MIDs are selected and reserved before server pause or SDP. probator and every MID committed to SDP remain reserved for the transport lifetime, including after consumer close; pre-SDP failure rolls back only its provisional reservation. Omitted MID never falls through to SDK map-size allocation; conflicts reject without touching existing consumers.
ownership.factory: One MF bundle/PeerConnectionFactory and one credit-driven non-platform ADM per engine, same factory/config injected into SFU. No platform/default ADM, device selection or microphone recording. PCM enters individual AudioSourceInterface tracks, never global RecordedDataIsAvailable.
ownership.sfuWrapper: Engine-owned PeerConnection wrapper requires the injected factory and bounds/cancels SDP/stats waits. Four SHA-pinned SDK Transport/Handler copies receive explicit streamId overloads during staging only; RemoteSdp separates MSID from RTP CNAME. Original upstream remains unchanged and original/staged hashes are recorded.
ownership.sfuServerDto: ICE ip/address aliases must agree; the native adapter normalizes to pinned SDK ip. Missing DTLS role means auto. Server SHA-1/SHA-224 fingerprints are validated but excluded from selection; at least one valid advertised SHA-256/384/512 fingerprint is required.
ownership.serverCleanup: The application owns server resource creation/deletion and room epochs. Local resource.close/engine.close do not send a server deletion RPC or wait for a server pause acknowledgement. On close, cancellation or failure, retire the matching purpose:'screen' server transport/producer/consumer IDs without touching purpose:'call'. Explicit enable/source gates still issue acknowledged pause/resume RPCs, which are not deletion.
ownership.availability: videoAvailable/audioAvailable/p2pAvailable/sfuAvailable describe compiled implementations only. availabilityScope is compiled-implementation-not-device-probe. runtimeQualified/audioRuntimeQualified are false and hardwareExecutionObserved is null; neither capabilities nor ready proves usable hardware, physical A/V sync or media performance.
ownership.qualification: Compilation and inert validation only until explicit permission. Do not call createEngine in current probes.
